page.layout: One column of running text, with a large woodcut initial at the start. Above the column, a centred title in capitals and italic, two lines long. A library stamp overlaps the right end of the title and is left out. No margin notes. No page number, running head or catchword. A signature mark stands at the foot.

main_text.head: IURISCONSULTUS, SIVE DE OPTIMO GENERE iuris interpretandi, [illegible, ~5 letters]. 1. c. Liber.
main_text.p: M[?]irifica profe-cto[?] & singularis quædam uis atque altitudo ingenij populo Romano, Dei concessu ac munere tributa est: qui & ad eas solas artes, contemptis ceteris animum adiecit, quæ solæ ad rem omnium maximā ac præclarissimam, Reipublicæ scilicet administrandæ scientiam, pertinerent: & in iis ipsis quarum studium se-mel amplexus est, ceteras omnes
[?] The first letter of the initial word is hidden by the woodcut initial and is read as M; the "cto" of "profecto" is uncertain.

page.notes: The woodcut initial is an ornamental N-like letter. Its first letter is read as M from the following letters "irifica". The library stamp (Biblioteca Nazionale Vittorio Emanuele, Roma) is excluded. The handwritten or stamped marks over the title words "Hanm." and "Lenm." are unreadable and marked as illegible. The title line "1. c." may be misread. The long s is written as s throughout. Line-end hyphens are kept as printed; "Reipublicæ" and "singularis" have no printed hyphen and are written whole.
